# MindAttic.Tickets — User Stories
> ✅ done (shipped & tested) · 🟡 partial · ⬜ planned. Every ✅ cites the test.
> Personas: **Dev** (the developer running the workspace), **Agent** (an AI agent working in a repo).

## Epic A — Ticket log
- **M.TIX-US-A1 ✅** As an Agent, `workflow ticket new` appends a ticket with the next free ID and
  changes nothing else in the file, so logging work never disturbs the stories. *(verified by
  `Add_takes_the_number_after_the_highest_existing_id_never_filling_a_gap`,
  `Add_inserts_only_one_line_and_leaves_the_rest_of_the_file_byte_identical`,
  `Save_preserves_crlf_line_endings_and_the_bom`,
  `Add_creates_the_tickets_section_at_the_end_when_missing`,
  `Add_refuses_when_the_tickets_section_is_not_last`, `Add_refuses_a_file_without_a_code`.)*
- **M.TIX-US-A2 ✅** As an Agent, `workflow ticket close` moves a ticket to closed or wont-do and only
  touches its Status and Ref. *(verified by `Close_changes_only_status_and_ref_of_that_row`,
  `Close_keeps_the_existing_ref_when_none_is_given_and_supports_wont_do`,
  `Close_throws_for_an_unknown_id`.)*
- **M.TIX-US-A3 ✅** As a Dev, `workflow ticket verify` fails when a committed row was deleted or
  reworded, or the table breaks the rules. *(verified by
  `CheckAppendOnly_rejects_a_deleted_or_reworded_row`,
  `CheckAppendOnly_allows_status_and_ref_changes_and_new_rows`,
  `Validate_flags_bad_ids_duplicates_wrong_prefix_vocabulary_and_dates`,
  `Validate_accepts_a_well_formed_table`.)*
- **M.TIX-US-A4 ✅** As a Dev, `workflow ticket list` shows tickets across every repo, filterable by
  repo, status, type and date. *(verified by `All_lists_tickets_across_repos`,
  `Parses_code_and_rows_and_unescapes_pipes`.)*
- **M.TIX-US-A5 ✅** As a Dev, `workflow codes check` reports duplicate project codes, repos without a
  ticket log, and malformed tables. *(verified by
  `Check_reports_duplicate_codes_missing_files_and_bad_tables`.)*

## Epic B — Workspace jobs
- **M.TIX-US-B1 ✅** As a Dev, `workflow repos status` shows each repo's local-only work and its GitHub
  state, resolving origins that predate a repo rename. *(verified by
  `Read_counts_uncommitted_unpushed_stashes_and_local_only_ignored_files`,
  `Read_of_a_clean_pushed_repo_has_no_local_only_work`,
  `IsRegenerable_separates_build_output_from_local_data`,
  `GitHubSlugFrom_handles_https_ssh_and_non_github`,
  `FetchAsync_paginates_and_records_archived_and_topics_by_lowercased_slug`,
  `WithRenamesAsync_resolves_a_stale_origin_through_githubs_redirect_and_skips_true_404s`.)*
- **M.TIX-US-B2 ✅** As a Dev, `workflow repos prune` previews archived or untagged repos and deletes
  only what's safe, so nothing that exists only on this machine is lost by accident. *(verified by
  `Plan_keeps_tagged_repos_and_marks_clean_archived_or_untagged_ones_safe`,
  `Plan_blocks_on_local_only_work_missing_github_copy_and_kept_dependents`,
  `Plan_does_not_block_on_a_dependent_that_is_itself_being_pruned`,
  `Scan_finds_unity_manifest_project_reference_and_slnx_paths_into_sibling_repos`.)*
- **M.TIX-US-B3 ✅** As a Dev, `workflow repos rollout tickets` gives every repo a USER_STORIES.md with
  a ticket log and a unique project code. *(verified by `DeriveCode_follows_the_codex_rule`,
  `DeriveCode_avoids_codes_already_taken`,
  `New_file_text_has_front_matter_and_an_empty_ticket_table_that_accepts_a_first_ticket`,
  `Repos_lists_only_git_folders_sorted_and_Containing_finds_the_enclosing_repo`.)*

## Priority backlog
1. Brainstorm: one naming theme for Orchestrator, Workflow, /autopilot (/work), /throttle, /unthrottle, /crossrepo and Launcher (triggers: workflow is a reserved keyword in Windows PowerShell 5.1, and the names come from different worlds). Leading idea, railway: Conductor (Orchestrator), Tickets (Workflow; CLI becomes 'tickets new'), crew (subagents), line (repo), car (worktree), /all-aboard and /last-stop (autopilot on/off), /throttle kept, /express (unthrottle), /transfer (crossrepo), Station (Launcher). Alternatives: aviation (Tower, Logbook, /clearance, Hangar); racing (PitWall, TimingSheet, /race, /pace-car, /green-flag, /open-track, Garage); everyday driving (ECU, Logbook, /floor-it, /off-road, Ignition); mission control (MissionControl, Manifest, /orbit, /coast, /full-burn, /spacewalk, LaunchPad); orchestra (keep Orchestrator, Score, /perform, /adagio, /allegro, /ensemble, Stage); military (CommandCenter, Orders, /campaign, /hold-fire, /full-assault, /joint-ops, Barracks); kitchen (expediter, order rail, /simmer, /rush); beehive, film set, harbor. Open questions: new project codes (M.FLOW would move), PowerShell 7 avoids the keyword clash anyway.
- **M.TIX-US-C1 🟡** As an Agent, `/commit` logs each commit through `workflow ticket` instead of
  hand-editing the table. Wired into the global `/commit` and the per-repo commit skills; it's an
  instruction, so no automated test proves an agent follows it.
- **M.TIX-US-C2 🟡** As a Dev, the Launcher has a Workflow menu item showing open tickets and repo
  status through this library (MindAttic.Launcher M.LNCH-US-E6). The library calls are tested here;
  the menu itself has no test yet.
- **M.TIX-US-C3 ⬜** As a Dev, `workflow codes fix` renames a duplicate project code and its ticket
  IDs, so a clash `codes check` reports can be resolved without hand edits.


## Epic D — The database: safety, concurrency and git
- **M.TIX-US-D1 ⬜** As a Dev, `workflow db restore` rebuilds data/workflow.db from the committed data/workflow.sql dump and proves it matches (row counts per table, `db check` clean, every view renders unchanged), so a corrupt or merge-conflicted binary is never data loss (M.FLOW-LAW-3). Today nothing reads the dump back.
- **M.TIX-US-D2 ⬜** As an Agent, my feature commits never carry data/workflow.db or data/workflow.sql; only `workflow db sync` commits them, and .gitattributes marks the db binary with a merge that keeps the working copy, so merging a worktree branch can't conflict on the database or roll it back to an older snapshot. Today ordinary commits sweep it in whenever it's modified.
- **M.TIX-US-D3 ⬜** As an Agent running alongside other autopilot agents, `workflow ticket new` from many processes at once hands out distinct IDs with none lost and no 'database is locked' failure, proved by a test that starts parallel writers against one database (and decides whether WAL beats today's journal_mode=DELETE with a 15s busy_timeout).


## Epic E — CLI output and coverage
- **M.TIX-US-E1 ⬜** As an Agent, workflow output piped or redirected (not a terminal) has no ANSI escape codes and honors NO_COLOR, so scripts and agents read plain text. Today `ticket list | cat` prints raw color codes around '0 ticket(s)', and help text keeps its underline codes even with NO_COLOR.
- **M.TIX-US-E2 ⬜** As a Dev, `workflow story list` is readable in an 80-column terminal: one line per story with ID, glyph, epic and the text cut to fit, instead of today's 20-character Story column that wraps each story over seven lines. `--json` is unchanged.
- **M.TIX-US-E3 ⬜** As a Dev, `workflow ticket list --search <text>` matches ID, summary and ref (case-insensitive) across the workspace, so finding a ticket doesn't mean piping --json through grep.
- **M.TIX-US-E4 ⬜** As a Dev, the commands agents run that have no CLI test yet are tested through the real `workflow` on a temp workspace: story new/edit/status, epic new, backlog add, ticket link (a refused cycle), ticket correct, db render, and db sync --no-push committing only the database files.


## Epic F — Viewer and canon
- **M.TIX-US-F1 ⬜** As a Dev, `workflow view` shows each ticket's and story's links (requires, blocks) and a ticket's history, and an ID in a summary or ref links to that item, so I can see from the page why something is blocked.
- **M.TIX-US-F2 ⬜** As a Dev, the Launcher's Workflow menu (M.LNCH-US-E6) has an 'Open viewer' item that runs `workflow view`, scoped to the repo I'm in.
- **M.TIX-US-F3 ⬜** As an Agent reading the canon, README.md and docs/BIBLE.md describe the database, not the markdown era: the intro and architecture diagrams say tickets live in SQLite, `ticket new` no longer claims 'only that one line changes', 'stories are still written by hand' goes, the glossary's 'Ticket log' stops pointing at the ## Tickets table, M.FLOW-LAW-2 stops repeating its trigger sentence, and the codex doctor passes.


## Epic G — Desktop UI (Workflow Desktop, WPF, WCAG 2.2 AA)
- **M.TIX-US-G1 ⬜** As a Dev, Workflow Desktop (src/MindAttic.Workflow.Desktop, WPF on net10.0-windows with MindAttic.Components.Wpf, the Orchestrator's look) opens from a Desktop and Start-menu shortcut that shows assets/logo.ico, which is also the exe and window icon, installed by deploy.ps1 to C:\Apps\MindAttic.Workflow.Desktop.
- **M.TIX-US-G2 ⬜** As a Dev or Agent, a ticket's approval (proposed/approved/rejected) and queue priority live in workflow.db (ticket_queue), recorded in its history, set through the library and 'workflow ticket approve|reject|priority', so the database stays the only store.
- **M.TIX-US-G3 ⬜** As a Dev, Workflow Desktop's Queue view lists every repo's open tickets in priority order; I approve, reject (with a reason; it closes wont-do) and reorder them by drag and drop or by keyboard (buttons, Alt+Up/Down), each change announced to screen readers.
- **M.TIX-US-G4 ⬜** As a Dev, Workflow Desktop's Tickets view lists every ticket in every repo, filterable by repo, status, type and approval, searchable by ID, summary and ref, sortable by column, with closed and wont-do tickets hidden until I show archived.
- **M.TIX-US-G5 ⬜** As a Dev, selecting a ticket opens a detail pane with its fields, history and links both ways (linked IDs focus that ticket, blocked state shown), where I close it, wont-do it, set its ref, correct its type with a reason and add or remove links.
- **M.TIX-US-G6 ⬜** As a Dev, Ctrl+N in Workflow Desktop files a new ticket (repo, type, summary, ref), remembering the last repo and type.
- **M.TIX-US-G7 ✅** As a Dev, Workflow Desktop shows agents' ticket changes within seconds without a manual refresh, and a Sync button runs 'workflow db sync' and shows its result.
- **M.TIX-US-G8 ⬜** As a Dev who relies on assistive tech, Workflow Desktop meets WCAG 2.2 AA: contrast, keyboard-only use, visible unobscured focus, names and roles, live regions, 200% zoom, high-contrast mode, 24px targets and a dragging alternative, proved by tests and an Accessibility Insights FastPass.


## Epic H — Better than Jira
- **M.TIX-US-H1 ⬜** As a Dev or Agent, I add append-only comments to a ticket (author, time, markdown), shown in its history, without rewording the ticket row.
- **M.TIX-US-H2 ⬜** As a Dev, a ticket has a markdown description separate from its one-line summary, and rewording the summary is a recorded correction with a reason, like CorrectType.
- **M.TIX-US-H3 ⬜** As a Dev, I tag tickets with labels and components and filter by them in the CLI and Workflow Desktop.
- **M.TIX-US-H4 ⬜** As a Dev, each ticket carries an effort estimate, seeded from the Orchestrator's TicketCosts actuals for similar tickets and editable, so the queue can sort by smallest effort from the database.
- **M.TIX-US-H5 ⬜** As a Dev, I see which agent, CLI or worktree is working a ticket and since when, from the Orchestrator's assignments, in the list and detail pane.
- **M.TIX-US-H6 ⬜** As a Dev, a Board view shows tickets in columns Proposed, Approved, In progress and Done, and moving a card (drag or keyboard) changes its approval or status.
- **M.TIX-US-H7 ⬜** As a Dev, I filter with a query language (repo:M.FLOW type:fix status:open label:ui 'text') and save named filters for reuse in the CLI and Desktop.
- **M.TIX-US-H8 ⬜** As a Dev, I select many tickets and approve, reject, close, label or reprioritize them in one action.
- **M.TIX-US-H9 ⬜** As a Dev, Ctrl+Z undoes my last Workflow Desktop action by writing a compensating, recorded change, never by deleting history.
- **M.TIX-US-H10 ⬜** As a Dev, Ctrl+K opens a command palette to jump to any ticket or story by ID or text and run any command by name.
- **M.TIX-US-H11 ⬜** As a Dev, Workflow Desktop shows and edits a repo's epics and stories (text, status, acceptance, evidence) and their implements links to tickets.
- **M.TIX-US-H12 ⬜** As a Dev, a dependency graph shows a ticket's requires chain both ways, with what's blocking it highlighted (and a text list for screen readers).
- **M.TIX-US-H13 ⬜** As a Dev, an activity feed shows every ticket change across the workspace as it happens, and a toast tells me when an agent closes a ticket.
- **M.TIX-US-H14 ⬜** As a Dev, a ticket lists the commits whose subject names it, in every repo, with links to them on GitHub.
- **M.TIX-US-H15 ⬜** As a Dev, a metrics view shows throughput, cycle time (opened to closed), and open tickets by repo and type over time.
- **M.TIX-US-H16 ⬜** As a Dev, I export a filtered ticket list to CSV or markdown.
- **M.TIX-US-H17 ⬜** As a Dev, filing a ticket offers a template per type (fix: symptom, cause, test; feature: story, acceptance) and warns when a similar open ticket already exists.
